items.claim: Two device claims over Ezek.40.1-Ezek.40.4 do not hold as stated. First, the disjunctive-stroke disclosure locates the verse's single occurrence inside the dateline clause of Ezek.40.1, which is a placement within the verse that the mark layer does not carry, and the same sentence then denies that any such placement can be had: a denial set behind a semicolon on a dateline-bearing claim. The count of one occurrence on Ezek.40.1 is itself correct. Second, the signal set asserts the vision speech device for the span, but the only speech in the span, at Ezek.40.4, is the 'he spoke to me' form; the counted 'he said to me' family has no member anywhere in chapter 40, its nearest members standing at Ezek.41.4, Ezek.42.13, Ezek.43.7 and Ezek.43.18.
items.both_sides: Onset side holds and is the strongest in this cluster: the year-bearing dateline, the hand idiom and the transport verb stand together in Ezek.40.1, which is also the fourteenth and last member of the book's dateline set, and the unit before it closes at Ezek.39.29 on the utterance signature with an open-section mark. Close side is content only: Ezek.40.4 ends on the charge to declare what is seen, and the first measuring verb follows at Ezek.40.5, beginning the eighteen-verse run of that verb that ends at Ezek.41.5. Because the close rests on a genre shift and not on a refrain, medium_low is the right confidence and should not move up; both defects above are disclosure defects and neither moves the seam.

items.claim: The hundred-cubit notice that closes Ezek.40.17-Ezek.40.19 at Ezek.40.19 is the first of three such notices and not a figure proper to this unit: the same outer-to-inner-court hundred cubits is stated again at Ezek.40.23 and at Ezek.40.27, each time closing a gate circuit. That recurrence crosses this unit's own close-side seam and argues continuity with the gate sequence beginning at Ezek.40.20, and it is not disclosed.
items.both_sides: Onset side is strong: Ezek.40.17 carries a transport verb with a location change out of the single named gate into the outer court, and what follows is court-level material, a pavement and thirty rooms. Close side is the contested one. Read one way, Ezek.40.19 states the court's width for the eastern and the northern sides together and so generalizes what Ezek.40.23 and Ezek.40.27 then state gate by gate, which keeps it with the court description; read the other way it is the closing distance notice of the gate circuit measured before it, in which case the court material is two verses and cannot stand alone. The first reading is better because the figure at Ezek.40.19 is given for two compass sides at once while the other two are given for one gate each, but the recurrence must travel as continuity evidence. Low confidence is right and the three-verse extent is defensible on the transport onset.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the six gate circuits of Ezek.40.20-Ezek.40.37 are one list that may not be cut inside it, or two groups divided by the court-change transport verb at Ezek.40.28.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Two corpus rules point opposite ways on the same span and the choice decides whether this stretch is one unit or two. The step-count contrast, seven at Ezek.40.22 and Ezek.40.26 against eight at Ezek.40.31, Ezek.40.34 and Ezek.40.37, favours the two-group reading, and a single unit would run eighteen verses, past the extent allowed even to a measured block; but the list-integrity rule is stated without that exception, so a ruling on it would settle the whole region rather than one pair of units.

What remains open is whether the adjacent seam verse must be carried in the structured evidence list at all, since some units here carry it, at Ezek.39.29, Ezek.40.19, Ezek.41.12 and Ezek.41.13, while others argue it in prose only, at Ezek.40.4, Ezek.40.17, Ezek.40.20, Ezek.40.38, Ezek.40.48, Ezek.41.4 and Ezek.41.5.
